# Welcome {.unnumbered}

::: {.hero}
**Two ingredients. A hundred homelands. One irresistible plate.**
:::

Chicken and rice may be the most widely shared meal on Earth. Nearly every
culture that grows rice and keeps poultry has, independently, arrived at the
same happy conclusion: that tender chicken and a pot of fragrant grains belong
together. What each culture does *next* — the spicing, the fat, the technique,
the ritual — is where the whole world opens up.

This is a cookbook, an atlas, and a small love letter to that pairing. Every
chapter takes one iconic dish, tells you where it comes from and why it matters,
and then hands you a recipe you can actually cook tonight.

## What's inside

- **17 dishes** spanning Singapore to the author's own kitchen, each with its
  story, a full ingredient list, and a step-by-step method.
- **Foundations** — how to cook rice that isn't gluey, plus the small handful of
  techniques (blooming spices, building sofrito, resting a bird) that show up
  again and again.
- **Open source** — the whole book is written in [Quarto](https://quarto.org).
  Spotted an error, or cook this dish differently in your family? The
  [Contributing](chapters/contributing.qmd) chapter shows you how to send a fix.

::: {.callout-important appearance="simple"}
## 🌾🚫 Gluten-free · 🥛🚫 Dairy-free
**Every recipe in this book is written to be gluten-free and dairy-free.** Where a
traditional ingredient contains gluten or dairy, the recipe names the swap inline
(gluten-free tamari for soy sauce, oil or plant-based butter for ghee and butter,
dairy-free yogurt, certified gluten-free bouillon). The one page to read first is
[The Cook's Toolkit](chapters/the-cooks-toolkit.qmd), which lists the standing
substitutions used throughout — so always check labels, since brands vary.
:::

## 🎵 Cooking soundtrack {#soundtrack}

Every good kitchen needs a little music. Hit play for the house playlist — kicking
off, as all great cooking must, with **the Chicken Dance on accordion**. It streams
straight from YouTube; tap play to start, and it'll roll on to the next track on its
own.

::: {.content-visible when-format="html"}

```{=html}
<div style="max-width:520px;margin:1.1rem auto 0.4rem;">
  <div style="position:relative;aspect-ratio:16/9;border-radius:12px;overflow:hidden;border:1px solid #d9c7a3;background:#000;">
    <div id="yt-player" style="position:absolute;inset:0;width:100%;height:100%;"></div>
  </div>
  <div style="display:flex;flex-wrap:wrap;gap:0.5rem;justify-content:center;margin:0.7rem 0;">
    <button type="button" onclick="window.ytCookAudio&&window.ytCookAudio.prev()" style="padding:0.4rem 0.9rem;border:0;border-radius:999px;background:#4b7f52;color:#fff;font:inherit;cursor:pointer;">⏮ Prev</button>
    <button type="button" onclick="window.ytCookAudio&&window.ytCookAudio.toggle()" style="padding:0.4rem 1.1rem;border:0;border-radius:999px;background:#c0392b;color:#fff;font:inherit;cursor:pointer;">⏯ Play / Pause</button>
    <button type="button" onclick="window.ytCookAudio&&window.ytCookAudio.next()" style="padding:0.4rem 0.9rem;border:0;border-radius:999px;background:#4b7f52;color:#fff;font:inherit;cursor:pointer;">Next ⏭</button>
  </div>
  <ul id="yt-tracklist" style="list-style:none;padding:0;margin:0 auto;max-width:520px;display:flex;flex-direction:column;gap:3px;font-size:0.95rem;"></ul>
  <p style="text-align:center;font-size:0.8rem;color:#999;margin:0.4rem 0 0;">Plays from YouTube. Add your own tracks in <code>index.qmd</code>.</p>
</div>

<script>
(function () {
  // 🎵 The cooking playlist — add { id, title, by } rows (YouTube video IDs) to grow it.
  var TRACKS = [
    { id: "_q9ufUJXqhI", title: "The Chicken Dance (Accordion)", by: "amarcordeon" },
    { id: "xXjF7HiDvyc", title: "The Chicken Dance",             by: "Lucy Riddett" },
    { id: "fUnhmh5BTmU", title: "Rice, Peas 'N' Chicken",        by: "Jay Scott" },
    { id: "30B5DYW-brQ", title: "Jambalaya (On the Bayou)",      by: "Creedence Clearwater Revival" },
    { id: "LdFqv3JBA4Q", title: "Chicken Lemon Rice",            by: "Priya Ragu" },
    { id: "DCQ44b02Anc", title: "Fried Rice",                    by: "G-Eazy" },
    { id: "hKyTc5fHGJY", title: "Genjer Genjer (Live on KEXP)",  by: "Dengue Fever" },
    { id: "5VaNmsGAgO4", title: "El Arroz con Pollo",            by: "Havana Cultura Band" }
  ];
  var player, current = 0, ready = false;

  function renderList() {
    var ul = document.getElementById("yt-tracklist");
    if (!ul) return;
    ul.innerHTML = "";
    TRACKS.forEach(function (t, i) {
      var li = document.createElement("li");
      var b = document.createElement("button");
      b.type = "button";
      b.textContent = (i + 1) + ".  " + t.title + " — " + t.by;
      b.style.cssText = "width:100%;text-align:left;padding:0.45rem 0.8rem;border:0;border-radius:8px;cursor:pointer;font:inherit;" +
        (i === current ? "background:#4b7f52;color:#fff;font-weight:600;" : "background:rgba(75,127,82,0.10);color:inherit;");
      b.addEventListener("click", function () { playIndex(i); });
      li.appendChild(b);
      ul.appendChild(li);
    });
  }

  function playIndex(i) {
    current = (i + TRACKS.length) % TRACKS.length;
    renderList();
    if (ready && player && player.loadVideoById) player.loadVideoById(TRACKS[current].id);
  }

  window.ytCookAudio = {
    toggle: function () {
      if (!ready || !player) return;
      if (player.getPlayerState() === 1) player.pauseVideo(); else player.playVideo();
    },
    prev: function () { playIndex(current - 1); },
    next: function () { playIndex(current + 1); }
  };

  function makePlayer() {
    if (!document.getElementById("yt-player") || player) return;
    player = new YT.Player("yt-player", {
      videoId: TRACKS[0].id,
      playerVars: { playsinline: 1, rel: 0, modestbranding: 1 },
      events: {
        onReady: function () { ready = true; },
        onStateChange: function (e) { if (e.data === YT.PlayerState.ENDED) playIndex(current + 1); }
      }
    });
  }

  window.onYouTubeIframeAPIReady = makePlayer;
  if (window.YT && window.YT.Player) makePlayer();
  else if (!document.getElementById("yt-iframe-api")) {
    var s = document.createElement("script");
    s.id = "yt-iframe-api";
    s.src = "https://www.youtube.com/iframe_api";
    document.head.appendChild(s);
  }
  renderList();
})();
</script>
```

:::

## How to read this book

You can read straight through for a culinary trip around the world, or jump to
whatever you're hungry for. If you're new to cooking rice, start with
[Rice 101](chapters/rice-101.qmd) — it will make every recipe that follows
turn out better.

::: {.callout-tip}
## A note on authenticity
There is no single "correct" version of any of these dishes. A recipe is a
snapshot of a living tradition, and every grandmother is right. Where a dish has
strong regional variants, this book notes them — and invites you to add yours.
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## With thanks
This book began as **Rebecca Greenwood's idea** — the inspiration and the spark that
got the whole project cooking. Watch this space: Rebecca will be adding some of her
own recipes down the line.

The title also tips its hat to the mockumentary
[***Juan Likes Rice and Chicken***](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=Fo0sN872oH0),
another of this project's inspirations.
:::

Now, put a pot on. Let's eat.
